items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: I was at the Uptown House before Charlie came to New York.

ctx.x: I wrote those songs for Charlie Barnet. "Mad About You" Walter Bishop Senior did the lyrics for. I wrote "Lover Man" and Jimmy Davis did the lyrics for that. Apparently, in those days, the only... There was a singer by the name of Willie Dukes. We always called him Day-to-Day, you know. But he was the only one that really made it on 52nd Street and sang with various groups. And he sang like Billie Holiday. Well, he started at Monroe's Uptown House, which I played now and then also; that's where Charlie Parker…

So... They didn't pay me for the arrangements for Larry Adler's "Begin The Beguine" -- Milt Gabler took both. Now, he recorded Eddie Heywood... You know, at that time Eddie Heywood was very hot with "Begin The Beguine." He had recorded Eddie Heywood on a 12-incher, and Eddie was the first one to record, to make a commercial record of "Lover Man." Actually, also Billie Holiday, because when he made the 10-incher (in those days, the 10-inch records were out), "Lover Man" was on the other side. Well, he inveigled…
